cases.purpose: Physically unplug and reconnect the PCIe component, then verify seating and post-cycle device detection without errors.
cases.test_command: Operator physically performs the PCIe unplug/reconnect cycle; agent may collect post-action lspci and kernel/BMC evidence but cannot perform the physical action.
risk_notes: Incorrect insertion or removal can damage the connector, card, cable, or system. The agent must not claim that the physical cycle occurred.
expected_evidence: Operator photos and record of the physical cycle.
Post-cycle PCIe enumeration and kernel/BMC error evidence collected by the agent.
blocked_conditions: No qualified operator is available to perform and document the physical PCIe cycle.

deepseek_original_review.ai_commands_summary: DeepSeek proposed i3c-tools/i3cdetect evidence, which does not validate the physical PCIe connector cycle.

cases.gpt_second_review_findings: The source testcase is a physical PCIe connector plug/unplug and seating check. The DeepSeek I3C command is a purpose mismatch. GPT classifies this as MANUAL ONLY; automation is limited to collecting evidence after an operator completes the physical action.

cases.purpose: Verify the CPU1 I3C controller/target response through the Wistron BMC or platform-management path according to the platform specification.
required_packages: BMC/I3C vendor tool and version, if required
cases.test_command: Run the vendor-provided read-only BMC/I3C probe command for CPU1 after the controller, bus, target address, and expected response are supplied; do not invent a generic i3cdetect command.
risk_notes: In this Wistron project I2C/I3C is BMC/platform-management scope. A wrong bus or address can probe the wrong device or affect management functions. Use read-only semantics unless the vendor specification explicitly requires otherwise.
expected_evidence: CPU1 target address response and device identity/data returned by the vendor tool.
Raw command output, exit status, and relevant BMC event/log evidence.
blocked_conditions: Missing platform specification, BMC controller/bus, target address, vendor tool/command, or expected response/criteria.
The supplied command is not confirmed read-only or its recovery behavior is unknown.

deepseek_original_review.ai_commands_summary: DeepSeek proposed host-side i3c-tools/i3cdetect and Linux sysfs/dmesg checks without the BMC target specification.

cases.gpt_second_review_findings: The testcase is not automatically BLOCKED by I3C ownership because Wistron defines I2C/I3C as BMC/platform-management scope. It is PARTIAL in PA Manager terms, but execution must stop until the BMC/I3C specification, controller/bus, target address, vendor tool/command, and expected criteria are provided.

cases.purpose: Physical inspection of component seating accuracy.
cases.test_command: Inspect all DUT components and confirm that each component is properly seated. Physical inspection and photographs; no automated command.
risk_notes: Physical action or visual inspection is required; a remote agent must not claim completion.
expected_evidence: Photos and operator inspection record confirming proper seating.
blocked_conditions: A remote agent cannot visually or physically verify component seating.
cases.gpt_second_review_findings: DeepSeek's NO direction is consistent with the physical nature of this testcase. GPT classifies it as MANUAL ONLY and limits the agent to recording operator-provided evidence; no remote execution command is proposed.
